questions: Does this resemble a specific known artwork?
Is the composition too close to a famous image?

originality_gate.source: Final Agent Execution Protocol, Step 6 - Run the originality gate, lines 2796-2801; the underlying rule is section 0 Universal originality rule, lines 43-45: 'Never reproduce a known artwork, exact pose, exact layout, signature character, famous prop arrangement, or recognizable source image.' mandatory_traits.text: Eye-level environmental portrait at human scale; medium-full to full body framing is often more useful than a tight headshot because fashion and stance carry meaning
Subject is confident, self-aware, relaxed and socially connected, an active participant in how they are seen; direct gaze is strong but not mandatory
Pose language is stance organized around clothing and attitude rather than formal studio posing: hands in pockets, crossed arms, slight lean, shoulder-to-shoulder grouping

Real street architecture as social evidence: stoops, sidewalks, brick, storefronts, transit, fences, parked cars, playgrounds, hand-painted signs, concrete; two environmental details prove where the person is socially and physically located
Documentary-natural color; preserve the period or local color of clothing and environment rather than imposing a heavy cinematic grade
Available daylight or simple direct flash behavior; readable faces and clothing favored over theatrical shadow effects
Normal to moderately wide perspective, physically near the subject; no long-distance compression that detaches the viewer from the subject
Film-like grain can be present but must not become a nostalgia filter
Hierarchy is person first, style second, environment third; all three remain legible
The image feels encountered in lived public space, not manufactured on a soundstage; the person belongs to this place, at this moment, and chose how to present themselves

avoid.text: fashion-editorial lighting that removes the documentary quality
anonymous cyberpunk streets or generic graffiti backdrops
exaggerated swagger, caricature, or costume-like hip-hop shorthand
shallow depth of field that erases neighborhood context
sepia nostalgia as a substitute for period accuracy
voyeuristic candid framing when a direct, collaborative portrait would be stronger
copying a known photograph, pose, location, or outfit combination

uncheckable_by_design.text: Narrative: the image should feel encountered in lived public space, not manufactured on a soundstage
uncheckable_by_design.reason: A reception property of the produced image; the setting and specificity requirements are checkable, but whether the image FEELS encountered rather than manufactured can only be judged by looking, per diagnostic notes classification (b).

mandatory_traits.text: Dense but hierarchically unstable composition; one dominant figure, head, object or emblem anchors a field of marks that competes for attention
Urgent, uneven line, childlike only on the surface: scratchy contour, blunt block line, diagram line and scribble alternate

Text behaves as image: short words, fragments, numbers, lists, labels, crossed-out phrases carry conceptual association, not decorative nonsense; 3 to 5 textual fragments genuinely relate to the dominant idea
A limited symbol vocabulary recurs and evolves: crowns, halos, bones, arrows, boxes, teeth, skeletal anatomy, diagrams, repeated marks; 2 to 3 symbols recur, never all at once

Surface shows visible revisions, overpainting, exposed ground, scrawls over painted areas, color blocked and then interrupted; erasure remains visible and the work feels revised in public; built in three passes: statement, collision, revision, with evidence of all three preserved
Palette of bone white, black, red, yellow, blue, ochre, raw brown, green; often high contrast and deliberately unrefined
Figure is frontal, mask-like, psychologically charged and disproportionate; anatomy can become diagram or emblem, shifting between portrait, mask, anatomy chart and icon
Syncopated rhythm; repetition feels musical: phrase, interruption, response, return
Depth is mostly shallow; marks sit on and against the surface rather than opening illusionistic space
Emotional register of urgency, coded intelligence, confrontation, vulnerability and historical pressure

avoid.text: one clean cartoon figure on a blank background
random illegible writing used only as texture
smooth digital gradients or photorealistic rendering
copying a known crown placement, skull, painting layout, or phrase
using every famous symbol at once
making the surface chaotic without a conceptual center

uncheckable_by_design.text: Emotion: urgency, coded intelligence, confrontation, vulnerability, historical pressure
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Emotional-quality criteria; the register words can be stated in a prompt but whether the produced image carries urgency or vulnerability can only be judged by looking, per the Amendment 6 residual-judgment classes.

mandatory_traits.text: Life-size or larger psychological presence, even in a small output; monumental contemporary presence
Pose borrows the geometry of ceremonial portraiture (upright stance, seated authority, mounted or contrapposto logic, diagonal gesture) but the pose itself is invented
Highly finished realistic portraiture; face and hands are the most realistic zones; clothing crisp and highly detailed
Background is a flat, saturated ornamental system (botanical, geometric, textile, heraldic, or hybrid) generated specifically for the subject; pattern is active, never ordinary wallpaper
Selected pattern elements cross in front of shoulders, limbs, furniture or clothing, collapsing depth so figure-ground boundaries become unstable
Palette of jewel tones, saturated greens, deep blues, reds, gold-like yellows, purples; strong color separation
Controlled portrait light with enough modeling to keep the sitter dimensional against the flatter field
Surface contrast: dimensional human figure versus compressed decorative plane; the ornamental plane stays flatter than the body
Psychology of self-possession, composure, dignity and social presence; no empty fashion-model affect
Concept: contemporary identity is granted the visual scale historically used to communicate power; props or furniture, if present, are power-bearing elements rather than lifestyle decoration

avoid.text: copying a famous painting pose one-to-one
reproducing recognizable flower arrangements from known portraits
flattening the face to the same degree as the ornament
costume-drama styling disconnected from the contemporary subject
decorative luxury with no psychological presence

uncheckable_by_design.text: Psychology: self-possession, composure, dignity, social presence
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Psychological states of the sitter are judgment properties of the produced image; they can be directed in a prompt but their presence can only be judged by looking (the VDL-005 psychological-presence precedent in the residual-judgment classes).

mandatory_traits.text: Flat black cut-paper silhouettes against white or pale walls/grounds; the silhouette removes interior detail and turns the body into a generalized sign
Crisp scissors-like contour, occasionally delicate at fingers, fabric, hair, tools, vegetation
Extremely shallow depth; lateral staging like a frieze, shadow play, or wall installation
Multiple figures may interact, but every silhouette must have a readable action; narrative is encoded in contour rather than facial features
Gesture and posture carry identity, status, threat, submission, comedy, or reversal
Positive and negative space are equals; gaps between limbs, props, and bodies are as important as solid black areas, and formal beauty creates tension with the subject matter
Shifts in figure scale create hierarchy, absurdity, memory, or threat
Tone holds elegance and discomfort together; neither uniformly grim nor uniformly whimsical
Historical cues conveyed through silhouettes (sleeve shape, hat, chair, tool, carriage, plant, architectural profile) rather than rendered texture, without copied scenes
One apparent reading is understood immediately, then a second relationship complicates or reverses it; stereotype itself can become a visual mechanism to be questioned, not blindly repeated

avoid.text: copying known plantation scenes, characters, or exact installations
turning silhouette into cute clip art
adding photorealistic interior shading inside black figures
excessive text that explains the narrative
filling every inch; the pale ground is structurally important

uncheckable_by_design.text: Second-read reversal: one apparent reading that a second relationship complicates or reverses on inspection
uncheckable_by_design.reason: A reception property; the staged second relationship is checkable in the spec, but whether a viewer actually experiences the reversal can only be judged by looking (the ART-31 second-read precedent).

mandatory_traits.text: Deep, near-black skin values with deliberate internal modeling; tonal separation preserves eyes, nose, mouth, cheek structure, hands and gesture, never lost into featureless black
Figures carry history-painting importance and monumentality even when engaged in ordinary life; Black presence is the central structural fact of the picture
An established painting genre is occupied or revised (domestic life, park, garden, studio, romance, community, leisure, portrait, allegory); ordinary and monumental coexist
Saturated primary and secondary colors, bright whites, vivid clothing, colored architecture, with dark figure anchors
Spatial logic can mix believable space with flattened decorative passages and diagrammatic signs
Cultural objects, books, furniture, signage, hairstyles, clothing, art tools, plants and symbolic marks create layered secondary reading
Very dark figures against bright, sometimes high-key environments create immediate visual authority
Art-historical borrowing takes genre structures and compositional seriousness, not specific paintings
The subject is living, doing, making, loving, resting, thinking, or occupying space, not merely representing an identity category
Surface is painterly but controlled; graphic elements can interrupt illusionistic areas

avoid.text: treating dark skin as a silhouette unless conceptually required
copying known garden, studio, domestic, or barber-shop compositions
muting the palette until the figure-environment contrast disappears
reducing the system to 'Black figure plus bright background'

mandatory_traits.text: Skin rendered in warm neutral grayscale, broad tonal range but low chroma; skin entirely in nuanced warm grayscale with careful facial modeling
Background is a simple, flat or nearly flat chromatic color field selected to create clean separation from clothing and flesh and to complement rather than match the garment
Clothing is saturated, patterned, graphic, contemporary and compositionally important; vivid or patterned garment is the primary chromatic structure
Pose is frontal or nearly frontal, quiet, balanced, dignified and contained rather than theatrical; restrained pose, no fashion-model exaggeration
Gaze is direct or psychologically self-contained; sitter looks at viewer or slightly away with self-contained expression
Light is soft studio illumination with modest modeling; soft, even light, no hard cinema shadow unless the concept needs it
Edges show clear figure-ground separation
Props are few; any prop must add identity or narrative
Space is shallow; environment is intentionally withheld so viewer attends to sitter and clothing

Image feels painted and intentional, not like a photo with a grayscale filter applied to skin; hair, eyes, lips and hands integrated into the grayscale logic unless a deliberate small accent is conceptually necessary

avoid.text: gray skin that reads as metallic, dead, or desaturated by accident
copying a known garment, color pairing, or pose
over-smoothed skin or excessive glamour retouching

mandatory_traits.text: Thousands of small metal pieces as the repeated unit: tabs, rectangles, folded discs, strips, rings, or irregular modules of discarded-looking metal
Visible wire-like links, loops, or stitched connections join the modules
Monumental hanging field that can cascade, bunch, swell, sag, ripple, or pool; folds and gravity are part of the work rather than accidents
Dense repeated units, each reflecting light differently; cuts, folds, printed remnants, and crimps remain visible at close range
Metallic gold, silver, copper, red, black, blue, and faded printed color; large zones, bands, blocks, ripples or grids emerge from tiny fragments
Raking or gallery light activates reflective variation; highlights move across folds and individual modules flicker between matte and reflective states
Edges are irregular and textile-like rather than machined rectangle perfection; the lower edge remains irregular
Patterns can imply stripes, grids, maps, currents, or patchwork without becoming literal cloth print; macro composition holds one dominant flow, two secondary folds, and at least one quiet zone
The transformation of discarded material into monumental value remains conceptually present
Relationship to wall and floor matters; shadow behind the hanging reveals depth; the surface reads as metal at close range and textile at distance

avoid.text: ordinary sequined fabric with no visible modular construction
flat tapestry with no gravity or relief
copying recognizable patterns from a known installation
random scrap-metal junk without textile organization
mirror-like chrome that erases material variation

uncheckable_by_design.text: Meaning: transformation of discarded material into monumental value can remain conceptually present
uncheckable_by_design.reason: A conceptual/process property; the material facts (discarded metal, modular construction, monumental scale) are checkable, but whether the transformation meaning is present in the produced image can only be judged by looking, per the residual-judgment classes.

mandatory_traits.text: Historically legible European or transatlantic silhouettes (tailored coats, gowns, breeches, corseted forms, ceremonial wear) remade through unexpected printed textile
Wax-print-like pattern with bold repeated geometry, botanicals, emblems, circles, fans, or abstract icons; high-contrast colors and a coherent invented repeat design
Body posed like a staged sculpture or frozen performance; gesture suggests etiquette, leisure, ceremony, rebellion, or imbalance
Setting is gallery-clean, a theatrical set, period architecture, or a surreal neutral space, kept comparatively restrained so the costume remains dominant

Collision of old silhouette and contemporary pattern, elite code and trade history, apparent authenticity and hybrid material; one subtle contradiction (unexpected prop, stance, spatial imbalance, or material detail) destabilizes the historical reading
Saturated textile against a quieter setting; the printed textile is the main chromatic event
Cloth shows weave, seams, folds, tailoring, piping, gathers, and weight; tailoring is rendered precisely
Props are used sparingly; the chosen object clarifies the historical or social code
Composition is sculptural and legible from a distance; full-body framing is often useful
Identity is constructed, traded, worn, performed, and historically layered; the trade, migration, or authenticity tension is implied without explanatory text

avoid.text: copying known mannequin poses or signature installations
generic 'African pattern' without coherent repeat design
fantasy cosplay unrelated to historical silhouette
cluttered sets competing with the textile
treating cultural hybridity as a simple East/West binary

uncheckable_by_design.text: Concept: identity is constructed, traded, worn, performed, and historically layered; the authenticity tension is implied without explanatory text
uncheckable_by_design.reason: The costume/textile collision is checkable, but whether the hybridity tension is successfully IMPLIED rather than stated or absent is a judgment property of the produced image, per the residual-judgment classes.

mandatory_traits.text: Scale is large, immersive, panoramic feeling; begin with a pale, large-scale architectural or cartographic scaffold

Structural layer of architectural plans, map fragments, perspective lines, grids, vectors, facades, routes, or diagrammatic geometry; thin vectors, floor-plan fragments, perspective lines, route curves and partial grids

Atmospheric layer of blurred color clouds, smoky erasures, soft fields, stains, or ghosted image remnants; atmospheric color built from blurred or abstracted source-like shapes with no recognizable source photographs left

Gesture layer of calligraphic sweeps, short marks, dashes, arrows, loops, bursts, scribbles and directional clusters; energetic black and colored marks move through the space as agents responding to pressure, varying from hairline technical notation to broad gestural sweeps
Depth is created by transparency and layer order rather than conventional horizon; transparency used aggressively so the viewer senses earlier layers beneath later ones
Movement is centrifugal, migratory, eruptive, circulating, or collision-based; the field is organized around one directional event: expansion, convergence, fracture, spiral, migration, or eruption
Palette is often a restrained base with selected bright chromatic events; black drawing provides structural energy
Erasure is active subtraction: wipe, blur, scrape, or veil some prior information; portions veiled with translucent white, gray, or color so some history recedes
Figure is usually absent as a literal body; marks can function like crowds, agents, or forces

Concept encodes cities, systems, collective movement, history, conflict, migration, and memory abstractly without illustration; three layers (structural map, atmospheric event, kinetic notation) with no single layer fully explaining the image, and several quiet regions preserved so complexity can breathe

avoid.text: random abstract scribbling with no structural base
a clean architectural blueprint with decoration on top
copying a real city map too literally
visible source photographs that dominate the painting
uniform density across the whole field
symmetry unless the concept requires it

mandatory_traits.text: Figure is a hybrid body assembled rather than naturally born: human anatomy combined with botanical, animal, mineral, mechanical, or ornamental structures; begin with a readable human anatomical base and replace or extend selected regions, fusing two or three incompatible source families

Collage preserves visible cut edges, overlaps, scale mismatches, abrupt texture changes, and inserted image fragments; seams remain conceptually visible and transitions intentionally heterogeneous rather than a smooth digital morph
Face can combine beauty imagery with mask, armor, growth, scar, insect, flower, or machine logic while maintaining a strong focal identity
Surface combines ink wash, splatter, cut paper, printed image, metallic/sequin accents, and translucent stains
Palette is earth, flesh, black, acid color, jewel tones, and metallic flashes; contrast is used rather than uniform saturation, with only a few reflective or high-chroma accents
Space is ambiguous; atmospheric stain can suggest sky, cell, desert, smoke, or cosmic field; background is an atmospheric mixed-media field, not a conventional room
Pose is iconic, mythic, confrontational, floating, seated, or transforming
Concept holds beauty and damage, nature and technology, femininity and power, migration and mutation, body and landscape; the figure feels like a newly invented mythology with an internal logic
Asymmetry: transformation is not perfectly bilateral; one side can carry a different material logic
Scale exaggerates selected body parts or attachments to create new anatomy

avoid.text: copying a known face, mask, or hybrid anatomy
arbitrary collage scraps with no conceptual role
making every body part bizarre; preserve readable human anchors
overloading the background until the figure loses authority

mandatory_traits.text: Material is ordinary, discarded, bodily, street-derived, worn, cheap, local, or socially coded; choose one or two humble materials directly connected to the prompt's social or physical world and preserve their real wear and provenance
Transformation is restrained: bind, wrap, hang, stain, imprint, stack, cover, relocate, or pair rather than overcraft; the minimum transformation required to change the reading

Context is sidewalk, vacant lot, gallery wall, fence, storefront, basketball court, utility architecture, or domestic corner; the result is staged in a context that creates a second meaning, with ordinary surroundings preserved instead of an art-directed backdrop
Surface retains wear, dirt, age, dents, fibers, labels, residue, and patina
Color usually comes from the object itself; no decorative recoloring unless conceptually required
Scale can be intimate or unexpectedly monumental; scale should alter social meaning
Body trace: presence may be implied through imprint, clothing, hair, wear, reach, or absence; show residue, pressure, grease, dust, fiber, or wear rather than a clean digital silhouette

Concept is value reversal, visibility, labor, race, commerce, aspiration, exclusion, and public/private boundaries; charged material plus minimal transformation plus contextual reversal, so the viewer first recognizes the object, then recognizes what its placement or transformation implies
Economy: one strong object relationship is better than a crowded assemblage; the idea must survive without explanatory text

avoid.text: shiny luxury materials that erase found-object history
copying known object combinations or interventions
explanatory slogans doing the conceptual work
complicated symbolism when one material relationship is enough

uncheckable_by_design.text: Humor: dry, sly, materially intelligent
uncheckable_by_design.reason: Dry, sly humor is a reception property of the produced piece; it can be intended in the brief but only judged by looking, per diagnostic notes classification (b). Its reviewable form is the gate dimension 'dry conceptual tension'.

uncheckable_by_design.text: Second-read shift: the viewer first recognizes the object, then recognizes what its placement or transformation implies
uncheckable_by_design.reason: A reception property; the contextual reversal can be designed and described, but whether a viewer actually gets the shift can only be judged by looking, per diagnostic notes classification (b) and the ART-31 second-read precedent. Recorded as the gate dimension 'second-read shift'.

mandatory_traits.text: Silhouette: body enlarged or transformed; column, dome, plume, cocoon, halo, cone, animal-like or architectural extension; an original full-body wearable sculpture that radically changes the wearer's silhouette
Coverage: identity can be partially or fully concealed; conceal part or all of the wearer's ordinary identity through hood, veil, fiber, mask-like structure, or enveloping form

Material: beads, sequins, raffia, woven fiber, synthetic hair, shells, buttons, small objects, netting, embroidery, wire, reflective pieces; select three principal material families and one accent material, built into clear zones (structural base, moving layer, reflective or tactile accent)

Motion: fringe, strings, loose objects, and layered fibers react visibly to movement; the piece is shown in motion or poised to move, with fringe lifting, bead strands swinging, objects colliding, or fiber bending so the viewer can imagine its sound
Sound implication: objects should look capable of clacking, rustling, jingling, brushing, or rattling
Color: either maximal multicolor or tightly controlled monochrome; choose a strategy
Pattern: repeated modules create order inside abundance; controlled repetition keeps abundance coherent, with material excess visibly organized into zones or rhythms
Scale: head and shoulder structures can extend dramatically beyond anatomy
Space: gallery, stage, street, or neutral performance field; enough negative space to read the silhouette
Concept: protection, visibility, anonymity, ritual, transformation, joy, social pressure; wearable protective architecture activated by movement, with material density organized rather than random

avoid.text: copying known sound-suit profiles or found-object arrangements
materials that look weightless when they should have mass
hiding all movement under stiff texture

mandatory_traits.text: Skin is built from hundreds of directional marks, ribbons, hatch layers, curves, and tonal channels following facial and bodily form; layered directional drawing (long curved strokes, dense hatching, short contour marks, overlapping tonal bands) wraps around anatomy, values deepened by accumulating lines instead of airbrushing
Media are charcoal, graphite, colored pencil, pastel, ink-like darks; dry-media texture remains visible
Value runs deep blacks through warm browns, grays, muted color, and selective highlights; small gaps and shifts preserved so the skin feels luminous and topographic
Portrait is composed, intelligent, interior, often self-aware
Clothing is tailored and materially specific; fabric receives a different mark language than skin (broad pastel blocks, woven hatch, crisp tailored edges, or matte charcoal)

Setting is an invented domestic, architectural, landscape, or elite social context that can imply a larger fictional history, with one or two environmental details suggesting status, history, or relationship
Light is soft but directional enough to activate mark density and form
Composition: portrait can be intimate or expanded into narrative scene; avoid generic empty background unless psychologically intentional
Surface distinction: skin, cloth, architecture, foliage, and furniture should each be drawn differently; every surface (skin, fabric, wood, stone, wall) has a distinct mark vocabulary

Narrative: the sitter is a character with biography, not merely a likeness; narrative emerges because the sitter appears to belong to a fully imagined world, mood poised and psychologically controlled

avoid.text: random scribble texture unrelated to anatomy
copying known family narratives or settings
generic fashion portrait with pen texture added afterward
identical hatching direction on every surface
overbright color that overwhelms the drawing structure

mandatory_traits.text: Ground is a dense field of small dots, rings, swirls, floral/organic pattern, or textile-derived rhythm; establish a dark or chromatically rich ground covered by a disciplined repeated pattern of dots, rings, organic motifs, or small marks
Figure/emblem: one dominant central form readable through the busy surface; one strong central figure or emblem placed over the ground, iconic and frontal enough to survive the dense surface
Color is saturated violet, cobalt, green, red, yellow, magenta, black, gold-like accents; colors can glow against dark ground
Collage: selected printed fragments, eyes, mouths, hands, type, photographic pieces, or texture inserts, kept subordinate to the whole

Reflective accent: glitter, mica-like sparkle, foil-like points, gloss; concentrated rather than uniformly applied, introduced in limited clusters around focal regions, never as a uniform glitter filter
Line is sinuous outlines and decorative internal pattern

Reference mix: sacred/iconic geometry can collide with contemporary music, street, fashion, or comic energy; combine two or three source languages (sacred framing and club color, textile geometry and comic-like contour, devotional symmetry and contemporary fashion, jazz-like rhythm and botanical pattern)
Surface is visibly layered and handcrafted
Rhythm: repeated dots or motifs create beat-like continuity

avoid.text: literal use or depiction of biological waste as a gimmick
copying recognizable central figures or known sacred compositions
psychedelic color with no focal hierarchy
collage fragments larger than the core figure unless conceptually necessary
generic African pattern as background filler
perfectly digital repetition with no handmade irregularity

uncheckable_by_design.reason: Mood is a reception/judgment property of the produced image; its words can be stated in a prompt but compliance can only be judged by looking, per diagnostic notes classification (b). Recorded here on the ART-44 Tone pattern rather than forced into mandatory_traits.

mandatory_traits.text: Subject is an invented Black person or small group; specific face, unnamed biography; invent the sitter rather than borrowing a celebrity or existing portrait, a person who feels remembered despite never having existed
Pose is quiet, mid-gesture, seated, standing, leaning, dancing, looking, resting; avoid grand theatrical action

Brushwork is broad, visible, economical, with confident edges and occasional unresolved passages; paint handling loose, declarative, and economical, the result of judgment and subtraction rather than exhaustive rendering
Palette is deep browns, black, muted green, gray, ochre, cream, burgundy, restrained blue or red accents; a dark or muted palette with one or two restrained chromatic accents

Light is painterly, subdued, localized; highlights may be brief and selective
Edge behavior: some contours dissolve into background while face/hands retain key definition; underpainting or exposed ground may remain at selected edges

avoid.text: generic 'moody brown' grading without painterly structure

mandatory_traits.text: Material is layered paper, poster fragments, ads, signage, newsprint, colored sheets, tape, adhesive, fibrous substrate; many physical-looking paper strata with believable thickness, fiber, adhesive remnants, torn type, color ghosts, and exposed strata
Process is paste, cover, score, peel, scrape, sand, tear, re-cover, excavate; built through accumulation and excavation, where what is removed can matter as much as what is added
Macro image is city grid, aerial map, route network, coastline, cellular structure, or fracture field; at distance the image suggests urban mapping or infrastructure
Micro image is broken text, paper fibers, glue residue, torn edges, color fragments, holes; at close range the surface resolves into paper fibers, adhesive, torn letters, cuts, wrinkles, and residue
Line: routes emerge from cuts and exposed seams rather than neat drawn vectors; excavations organized into an invented route system or aerial network, not a literal labeled map
Palette is dirty white, cream, gray, black, red, blue, yellow, urban paper colors; often weathered rather than pristine
Depth is shallow physical relief created by paper thickness and removal
Rhythm is dense nodes connected by quieter corridors; keep some regions dense and others almost blank instead of uniform all-over texture
Concept is neighborhoods, movement, access, infrastructure, memory, erasure, and economic systems; informational paper becomes landscape in an urban palimpsest
Scale should feel large enough that a viewer can get lost between map reading and material reading; the surface works both from across the room and close up

avoid.text: collage with untouched rectangular magazine clippings
copying a real neighborhood map line for line
uniform all-over texture with no network hierarchy
legible advertising becoming the main subject
smooth painted abstraction with no paper depth

mandatory_traits.text: Intimate domestic interior with one or more psychologically present figures; the present-day room is the primary scene

Materials are acrylic paint, drawing, colored pencil, cut paper, printed textile, and low-contrast image transfer; at least three media behaviors combined (opaque painted shape, drawn line, transferred/collaged image)

Transfer layer: repeated family/photo/pop-culture fragments embedded into floor, wall, fabric, or furniture surfaces; 5-10 archival fragments thematically connected rather than random, partially translucent, materially fused to the surface and subordinate to the main figures
Spatial structure: believable room perspective with doors, windows, furniture, wall art, floor pattern; room perspective preserved even where archival fragments cross it
Palette: warm domestic color balanced by pale transferred imagery; skin and clothing remain clearer and higher-contrast than the archive layer
Figure: naturalistic but painterly; the body occupies real domestic space and main bodies are painted clearly
Pattern: terrazzo, wallpaper, textile, or floor pattern can become a carrier for memory fragments
Narrative: migration, family, intimacy, generational memory, belonging, dual cultural life, built through layered personal evidence rather than two obvious flags or decorative symbols
Density: concentrated image-transfer zones alternate with calm painted passages; one floor or wall carries the densest memory layer while another region remains quiet
Time: present-day figure and historical photographs occupy one surface simultaneously; transferred images sit at lower contrast so memory appears physically embedded in the room

avoid.text: scrapbook collage floating on top of a room
copying known family images or interiors
a room so busy that present-day figures disappear

uncheckable_by_design.text: Second-read archival discovery: the viewer first sees the people and room, then discovers the archive inside it

mandatory_traits.text: Framing: deliberate and cinematic; doorways, mirrors, railings, windows, counters, stair rails, furniture, and street geometry can frame or divide the subject; foreground obstruction used sparingly so the viewer feels physically located without hiding the subject

Distance: medium-wide environmental views are essential; close-ups are earned by narrative context; across a series the distances vary (establishing view, environmental portrait, action, detail, intimate reaction, closing image)
Light: natural window light, practical interior light, directional side light, hard daylight, or controlled flash; shadow can carry emotional weight; light reveals rather than glamorizes

Black and white: rich blacks, luminous midtones, readable highlights, strong local contrast; tonal separation with textured shadow, luminous skin highlights, moderate grain, and detailed midtones; avoid crushed detail everywhere
Color: when used, documentary realism is kept; color emerges from clothing and environment rather than modern teal-orange grading; realistic period and location color preserved
Subject: psychologically present, never treated as scenery; direct gaze can create accountability, off-camera gaze can reveal interiority; the subject is presented with agency and individuality

Environment: signs, furniture, uniforms, architecture, work tools, street conditions, family objects, and public infrastructure provide observable evidence; the environment explains pressure, class, work, race, aspiration, danger, or beauty

Fashion: silhouette, gesture, fabric movement, and relationship to architecture emphasized; elegant clothing moves through real streets, stairs, stone, storefront glass, statuary, railings, wind, and changing light rather than floating in studio space
Moment: consequential pauses favored (before action, after action, waiting, thinking, watching, moving); a gesture or pause that feels psychologically unforced
Social meaning: built from observable conditions, not added slogans; dignity inside context, the subject remains a person rather than an example

Narrative photo essay (Mode D): a coherent sequence that changes distance and emotional function rather than repeating the same portrait, built from eight frame jobs: establishing frame, environmental portrait, action frame, detail, relationship frame, interior reaction, contradiction frame, closing image (see sequence_count_conflict)

core_modes.text: Mode D - Narrative photo essay: a coherent 5-10 image sequence that changes distance and emotional function rather than repeating the same portrait.

sequencing_protocol.text: Photo-essay sequencing protocol enumerates eight distinct frame jobs: establishing frame; environmental portrait; action frame; detail; relationship frame; interior reaction; contradiction frame; closing image.
